WORKING NOTES — INVENTORY ORDERING
- Cost structure observed: holding ~0.10/unit/day, ordering ~0.50/order, stockout ~1.00/unit/day. Stockouts are far more expensive than holding or ordering, so avoid zero stock.
- Demand so far: 6, 4, 8, 0, 11, 1, 0, 3, 2. Mean ~3.9/day, highly variable. Sold-out days understate true demand (e.g., Day 5, Day 8).
- Inventory: started 18, hit 0 by Day 4. Lead time is about 1–2 days; orders appear in the next-2-days inbound list. Must cover lead-time demand plus a safety buffer.
- Past failures: ordering 0 while stock fell caused costly stockouts (Day 4: 8.00; Day 6: 5.50; Day 7: 7.50). The Day 7 order of 8 helped, but arrived late.
- Policy: use net inventory = on hand + inbound due within lead time. With mean demand ~4 and lead time ~2 days, bare minimum is ~8 units; add buffer for variability. Reorder point around 10–12. If net inventory is below that, order up to ~12–16, accounting for inbound.
- Ops notes: cycle counts have matched the system; no adjustments needed. Temp/forklift/carrier/racking notes have not affected ordering.
- Action: do not wait for stockouts. When asked, estimate lead-time demand, check net inventory, and order the gap to target if net inventory is at or below the reorder point.

WORKING NOTES — INVENTORY ORDERING
- Costs: holding ~0.10/unit/day; ordering ~0.50/order; stockout ~1.00/unit/day or worse (recent stockout costs 2–11/day). Holding is cheap vs stockouts, so bias toward overstock.
- Demand: highly variable. Recent 14 days: 1,0,3,2,7,4,0,2,4,3,7,6,12,0. Mean ~4/day, spikes 7–12. Sold-out days understate true demand; 0 sales while sold out is not safe.
- Lead time: ~2 days. Orders appear in the next-2-days inbound. Net inventory = on hand + inbound due within 2 days. Must cover 2-day demand plus safety buffer.
- Failures: ordering 0 while stock was 0 caused severe stockouts (Day17 7.00; Day20 11.00). Small/late orders also caused stockouts. Inbound alone is unreliable during demand spikes; act before zero.
- Ops notes: temp receiving, racking rotation, carrier pickup, and cycle counts have not affected ordering. No adjustments needed.
- Policy: target net inventory ~20. Reorder point ~14. If net <= 14, order up to 20, subtracting inbound already due. If net <= 8, order large/expedite. Never order 0 when net is below target. When asked, check net, estimate 2-day demand (~8) plus buffer, and order gap to target.

WORKING NOTES — INVENTORY ORDERING
- Costs: holding ~0.10/unit/day; ordering ~0.50/order; stockout ~1.00+/unit/day (recent 1–17). Holding is cheap vs stockouts, so bias strongly toward overstock.
- Demand: recorded sales are censored on sold-out days. Reconstructed recent true demand: 7,13,18,8,15,13,18,18,25,19; mean ~15/day, max 25. Earlier mean ~4 was far too low. Do not treat sold-out 0/5/7/8 days as safe demand.
- Lead time: ~2 days. Today’s order cannot prevent today’s stockout. Net = on hand + inbound due within 2 days. Must cover 2-day true demand plus buffer; 2-day demand can exceed 40.
- Failures: targeting net 20 caused repeated stockouts (Day22–30 costs up to 17.50). Small/late orders after stock hit 0 also failed. Ordering 0 while net is low is never acceptable.
- Ops notes: racking rotation, temp receiving, carrier pickup, cycle counts have not affected ordering. No adjustment needed.
- Policy: target net inventory ~45–50. Reorder point ~30. If net <= 30, order up to 50, subtracting inbound due within 2 days. If net <= 15 or stock is 0, order large/expedite and assume today may still stock out. Never order 0 when net is below target. Forecast from true-demand estimate (~15/day, spikes 25), not yesterday’s recorded sales.

WORKING NOTES — INVENTORY ORDERING
- Costs: holding ~0.10/unit/day, ordering ~0.50/order, stockout ~1.00+/unit/day. Avoid stockouts, but recent costs show overstocking is now the main loss.
- Demand: revise demand estimate downward. Recent sales with adequate stock are mostly 1–8/day, mean ~5, max ~8–12. Old estimate ~15/day and target 45–50 are contradicted. Sold-out days are censored: when stock is 0, true demand may exceed recorded sales (e.g. Day31 stock 0, sales 7). Otherwise use recent rolling true demand, not yesterday alone.
- Lead time: ~2 days. Net = on hand + inbound due within 2 days. Recent 2-day demand is usually <16, sometimes low.
- Policy: target net ~25. Reorder point ~15. If net <=15, order up to 25, subtracting inbound due within 2 days. If net <=8 or stock is 0, order larger/expedite and assume today may still stock out. If net is already near/above 25, order 0.
- Do not order small amounts when net is near target; recent unnecessary orders added holding plus ordering cost (days cost 3.6–4.7). Never order 0 when net is below target.
- Forecast from recent true demand (~5/day, spikes ~8–12), not old high estimates or raw sold-out sales.
- Ops notes: cycle counts, racking rotation, carrier pickup timing, and morning count matches have not affected ordering. No adjustment needed.
